sources.title: Celeste Muñoz Martínez, Between divorces, thugs and healers: Race Tribunals in Spanish Guinea (2023)
sources.note: Full author-uploaded article directly read; Rubrica Contemporanea 12(23), pp. 229 to 249. Historical introduction, pp. 232 to 233, covers limited 1880 presence, Treaty of Paris in 1900, occupation through 1926, and 1902 judicial distinctions. Publisher PDF indexed but direct access failed.

sources.title: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Fang woven plate Djat, CE811
sources.note: Complete original museum catalogue read through indexed result; direct fetch failed. Production attributed to Bata district, second half of nineteenth century; collected during 1884 to 1886 expedition. Description and reasoned classification distinguish eating, pottery support and basketmaking. Fang expression is current catalogue spelling, not claimed nineteenth-century inscription.

sources.title: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Balengue comb, CE880
sources.note: Complete indexed original museum record read; direct fetch failed. Twenty-seven bamboo teeth, vegetable-fibre binding, 8.7 by 8.5 centimetres; collected 1884 to 1886. Catalogue describes grooming practices and intended parasite prevention; no efficacy claim is adopted.

sources.title: Museo Nacional de Antropología, carpenter’s plane CE805, Río Congüe
sources.note: Indexed original search result, first record CE805, identifies the tool, locality, second-half nineteenth-century date and Ossorio collection history. Full object technical description not accessible; do not infer blade type or exact method.

sources.title: Gonzalo Álvarez Chillida and Gustau Nerín, The formation of Equatorial Guinean elites during colonial rule (2018)
sources.note: Full original journal HTML read. Sections Jefes and Auxiliares y catequistas support coercive colonial intermediaries, Bata schooling, native catechists and interpreters. Later island family settlement policies are not generalized to early Río Muni.

sources.title: Claretian institutional biography, Joaquín Mª Sialo
sources.note: Indexed original full relevant passage checked: 1911 examination, Banapá arts-and-crafts school, printing since 1903, shoemaking, tailoring, carpentry, masonry, band and experimental farm. Direct fetch failed. Island example explicitly outside imported mainland polygon.

sources.title: Instituto Geográfico Nacional, Mapa de la Guinea Española, 1900, catalogue T0003571
sources.note: Full indexed official cartographic catalogue read; direct fetch failed. Depósito de la Guerra map at 1:500,000 with Río Muni inset at 1:20,000, 1900. Spanish title is an attested catalogue transcription, with literal English translation.

sources.title: United States Office of the Historian, Equatorial Guinea country history
sources.note: Directly read original page, Recognition section: independence from Spain 12 October 1968. Combined runtime reuse counted.

proposedOverrides.name: Spanish Guinea
proposedOverrides.summary: A mainland colonial claim expanded from limited coastal footholds into Río Muni.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: All three imported snapshots have bbox 9.369,1.100,11.079,2.137: mainland Río Muni. Bioko and other colonial islands are absent. The overview and island school passage state the distinction explicitly.
batchIdentityNotes.identity: A colonial label, not a unified ethnic civilization. Kept separate from existing equatorial-guinea, whose imported record begins in 1914. No alias association.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Fang along ncueng from the current museum catalogue, clearly modern orthography accompanying a nineteenth-century object; Spanish 1900 map title is the period witness. Neither is presented as an inscription on a household object.
batchIdentityNotes.access: Direct original journal full text and official independence page; direct author-uploaded history paper. Museum, IGN and Claretian biography evidence from complete indexed original passages; direct requests to those sites failed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: No foundation in 1878 or collapse in 1914 asserted. Collection dates 1884 to 1886 are not manufacturing dates. Occupation of mainland interior continued after this record.
